claims.text: The as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy has a coarse lamellar dual-phase microstructure.
The two phases include a soft ductile phase and a hard strengthening phase.
A brief anneal just below the primary hard-phase solvus followed by rapid quenching will refine the eutectic lamellae.
The proposed heat treatment will homogenize the eutectic lamellar microstructure.
Annealing for 5–15 minutes near 0.9 times the primary-phase solvus temperature will cause partial dissolution of coarse lamellae.
The short high-temperature anneal promotes diffusion-assisted homogenization at phase boundaries.
Rapid quenching freezes a finer lamellar morphology after partial dissolution.
The heat treatment enhances interfacial bonding between the ductile and strengthening phases.
Reduced interlamellar spacing increases dislocation pinning and thereby raises yield strength.
The finer lamellar morphology increases the spacing of obstacles for dislocation glide and thereby increases strength.
Improved phase-interface continuity and toughness reduce stress concentrations and enhance ductility.
The treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 10–20% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment will improve uniform elongation by a relative margin similar to the predicted strength increase.
Simultaneous strength and ductility improvement is expected only when the constituent phases remain stable during annealing.
The effect requires reduction of eutectic spacing without unwanted coarsening or formation of deleterious secondary phases.
The predicted effect applies under room-temperature, quasi-static mechanical loading.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility changes depends strongly on composition, temperature, annealing time, cooling rate, and initial cast microstructure.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator specifies reduced interlamellar spacing, whereas the mechanism says the finer morphology increases the spacing of obstacles for dislocation glide. Refinement would ordinarily mean more closely spaced obstacles, so the stated geometric link is internally inconsistent.
